glosses: Unclean; covered with or containing unpleasant substances such as dirt or grime.

examples.text: Despite a walk in the rain, my shoes weren't too dirty.
Many persons are more comfortable when they are dirty than when they are clean; but that does not recommend dirt as a national policy.

glosses: That makes one unclean; corrupting, infecting.

examples.text: Don't put that in your mouth, dear. It's dirty.

glosses: Morally unclean; obscene or indecent, especially sexually.

examples.text: At the reception, Uncle Nick got drunk and told dirty jokes to the bridesmaids.
We have quite a playful and fun relationship in general, but it’s still surprising how dirty our sex can be in the things we say or do or pretend. We often laugh about it afterwards.

glosses: Dishonorable; violating accepted standards or rules.

examples.text: He might have scored, but it was a dirty trick that won him the penalty.
The world 'as got me snouted jist a treat; Crool Forchin's dirty left 'as smote me soul.

The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable.[…]Partly, this is a result of how online advertising has traditionally worked: advertisers pay for clicks, and a click is a click, however it's obtained.

glosses: Corrupt, illegal, or improper.

examples.text: I won't accept your dirty money!

glosses: Out of tune.

examples.text: You need to tune that guitar: the G string sounds dirty.

glosses: Of color, discolored by impurities.

examples.text: The old flag was a dirty white.

glosses: Containing data needing to be written back to memory or disk.

examples.text: Occasionally it reads the sector into a dirty buffer, which means it needs to sync the dirty buffer first.
Notice that an asterisk has been added to the filename in the edit window tabs. This is a simple reminder that the file is “dirty” and needs saving.

glosses: Carrying illegal drugs among one's possessions or inside of one's bloodstream.

examples.text: None of y'all get into my car if you're dirty.

glosses: Used as an intensifier, especially in conjunction with \"great\".

examples.text: He lives in a dirty great mansion.

glosses: Sleety; gusty; stormy.

examples.text: dirty weather
Storms of wind, clouds of dust, an angry, dirty sea.
Rain type 17 was a dirty blatter battering against his windscreen so hard that it didn't make much odds whether he had his wipers on or off.

glosses: Of an alcoholic beverage, especially a cocktail or mixed drink: served with the juice of olives.

examples.text: dirty martini

glosses: Of food, indulgent in an unhealthy way.

examples.text: You can call it quick-and-dirty if you like, but there are billions of dollars out there riding on the supposition that fast food is not necessarily dirty food.

Dirty keto refers to an approach that follows the typical keto macro ratios, but the components include “dirty” foods like fast food, packaged convenience foods, processed meats, artificially sweetened diet sodas and sports drinks, and unhealthy […]

glosses: Of food, covered in an array of indulgent toppings.

examples.text: Lardo in Portland, Oregon, serves "dirty fries" topped with fried rosemary, peppers, lardons, and Parmesan.
Piled high and oozing all the trimmings, the dirty burgers here are decidedly good – spice things up with jalapeños, brie or a seriously sticky BBQ sauce.

glosses: Spreading harmful radiation over a wide area.

examples.text: a dirty explosion
a dirty bomb

glosses: Having the undercarriage or flaps in the down position.
Of an audio recording: containing unwanted noise.
Producing much ash.
In a dirty manner.

examples.text: to play dirty

glosses: To make (something) dirty.
To stain or tarnish (somebody) with dishonor.
To debase by distorting the real nature of (something).
To become soiled.

examples.text: The markers for the slow line signals have been arranged at cab level, but for the inner fast lines they have had to be kept low in the "six-foot", with the result that they tend to be badly dirtied by passing traffic.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: weniger sauber machen, schmutzig machen

glosses: To make something harmful, especially by the addition of some unwanted product.

examples.text: The factory polluted the river when it cleaned its tanks.

glosses: To make something or somewhere less suitable for some activity, especially by the introduction of some unnatural factor.

examples.text: The lights from the stadium polluted the night sky, and we couldn't see the stars.

glosses: To corrupt or profane

examples.text: But as for the cowardly, the faithless, the polluted, as for murderers, fornicators, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars, their lot shall be in the lake that burns with fire and sulphur, which is the second death.

glosses: To violate sexually; to debauch; to dishonour.
Polluted; defiled.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: weniger sauber machen, schmutzig machen

glosses: To make something dangerous or toxic by introducing impurities or foreign matter.

examples.text: This water is contaminated. It isn't safe to drink.

glosses: To soil, stain, corrupt, or infect by contact or association.

examples.text:
Shall we now
 Contaminate our figures with base bribes?
I would neither have simplicity imposed upon, nor virtue contaminated.
[Martin] Heidegger's repellent political beliefs do not contaminate his philosophical work.

glosses: To make unfit for use by the introduction of unwholesome or undesirable elements.

examples.text: Do not contaminate the peanut butter with the jelly.

glosses: To infect, usually of a deadly virus.
Contaminated.

examples.text:
And that this body conſecrate to thee,
By Ruffian Luſt ſhould be contaminate!

glosses: Dirty, sinful, wicked, gross, etc.

glosses: Rejeter des produits nocifs dans l’environnement.

examples.text: L'« éventrement » d'un supertanker menace la vie d'un petit équipage, mais pollue une fraction notable de la Manche ou de la mer du Nord.

glosses: Profaner et souiller, généralement un lieu saint.

examples.text: Polluer les choses saintes.
Polluer un temple.
Une église qui a été polluée.

glosses: Salir ses draps, ses vêtements, par une éjaculation nocturne et involontaire, dite pollution nocturne.

examples.text: La honte se lit sur ton visage… Alors tu as pollué tes draps cette nuit.

glosses: Se souiller du péché d’impureté.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: weniger sauber machen, schmutzig machen

glosses: Rendre sale.

examples.text: Prenez garde de ne pas salir ce plancher.
Je me suis sali les mains à manier des livres pleins de poussière.
Cet enfant s’est sali.
Les étoffes blanches se salissent vite.

glosses: Présenter à l’imagination des idées déshonnêtes.

examples.text: Ce conte, cette description salit l’imagination.

Quoi que dise la directive eCommerce, il n’y a quasiment plus rien qui relève de l’exercice de la liberté d’expression sur les plateformes centralisées lucratives, sinon une grotesque parodie qui salit le nom même de la liberté et nous en fait peu à peu perdre jusqu’au sens !
S’il reste aux républicains un brin ou deux de décence, ils exprimeront ouvertement leur désaveu pour l’homme indigne qui salit sa fonction et bafoue les règles.

glosses: Déshonorer quelqu’un par des propos, par des calomnies.

examples.text: Salir quelqu’un, salir la réputation de quelqu’un.

glosses: Se dit d’un homme qui a fait quelque action nuisible à sa réputation.

examples.text: En agissant de cette sorte, il s’est sali.

glosses: Se couvrir d’adventices, d’acrû, de plantes indésirables.

examples.text: Une fois les peuplements ouverts et en l’absence de semis, le parterre des coupes se « salit » (colonisation par les graminées, par les rejets de taillis…) et, peu de temps après, le terrain devient impropre à la germination des glands.

glosses: Gâter, salir.

examples.text: Souiller ses vêtements, ses mains de boue, de sang.

glosses: Rendre impure une personne ; profaner, violer une chose sacrée.

examples.text: C'est la pauvreté d'esprit qui purifie le cœur des ordures dont les richesses l’ont souillé.
Nul doute que le dieu pur, Apollon, ne s'entoure surtout de purificateurs. Le sang d'un monstre l’a souillé. Il lui faut, à lui comme à un être mortel, des cérémonies expiatoires.
Épargne-moi le récit de tes turpitudes, Igor ! Le sexe, c’est sale ! Tu devrais avoir honte. Tu souilles la robe que tu portes…

glosses: Avilir, flétrir, salir une personne, ses attributs, ses affects.

examples.text: Souiller sa gloire par des cruautés.
